title: What is known about 1RB---_1LC0LD_0RF0LD_0LE0RA_0LC1RA_1RC1RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1LC0LD_0RF0LD_0LE0RA_0LC1RA_1RC1RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, and probably never halting. From step 18 the run is the orbit of an explicit map on (tail, n). The tail is 1, Xk, Yk or Zk, and n is multiplied by 3/2 or 9/8 per pass. The map is proved in Lean's kernel for every tail and every n, except Zk with n < 12k+12, the only place where a halt can come from. Lean also checks the orbit: the first 3,000 passes from blank tape stay in the proved region (kernel; no halt in the first 10450 steps), and so do the first 105 (native_decide; 1016000 steps). The closest approach to the bad region was at pass 28 (n = 3,989, k = 5), still 55 times above the bound. A non-halting proof would need a bound on k in terms of n along the whole orbit, which is a Collatz-type question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The E-pass map, for all n
claims.text: With an E-event E> 0^6 (10)^n T (Ev n T): next T n gives the next E-event and the exact number of steps to it, for every tail T (1, Xk, Yk, Zk) and every n, except Zk with k = 0 or n < 12k+12. next_sound proves that the machine goes there in exactly that many steps. It rests on 83 case theorems (tail 1 by parity of n; X and Y by n mod 8, with a generic k and a few small k; Z by the parities of k and n), each a chain of symbolic-simulator segments and loops (three rounds of the 9/8 phase, or one round of the 3/2 phase) proved by induction. Axioms: propext and Quot.sound only.

claims.title: The blank tape reaches the map, and 3,000 passes stay inside it
claims.text: init_E: blank tape reaches the E-event (1, 0) after 18 steps. orbit_sound chains next_sound along the orbit. The kernel evaluates the first 3,000 passes: all inside the proved region, so no halt in the first orbitT 3000 > 10450 steps (no_halt_3k). The step count of pass 37, 20,999,239,576, is the one direct simulation finds.

claims.title: 10<sup>5</sup> passes, no halt in 10<sup>16000</sup> steps
claims.text: The same orbit check for the first 10<sup>5</sup> passes, evaluated by compiled code: no halt in the first 10<sup>16000</sup> steps.

claims.title: The E-pass map against direct simulation
claims.text: With an E-event E> 0^6 (10)^n T (n maximal): the tail T is always 1, Xk = 000 (10)^k 1, Yk = 11 (01)^k or Zk = 000 (10)^k 0001. The next E-event has n' = (3n+c)/2 for tails 1 and Zk, and n' = (9n+c)/8 for Xk and Yk. The new tail and c depend on the tail and on n mod 2 or n mod 8, and the index k changes by −2 to +1 or becomes 3k/2+3 or (3k+1)/2 (table in py/emap.py). The X and Y rules hold for all n ≥ 0, and Zk needs n ≥ 12k+12. Checked against direct simulation on a grid (every tail with k < 25 at 120 values of n each: 9,120 starts, no mismatch) and against the 200 rules measured independently by direct simulation. (Now proved in Lean, above.)

claims.title: The map against the run from blank tape
claims.text: The first E-event is (1, 0) at step 18. The E-events of the direct run up to 2.1·10<sup>10</sup> steps (38 events) each follow from the one before by the map; the last is (1, 48,351) at step 20,999,239,576.

claims.title: 10<sup>5</sup> passes inside the region where the map applies: the margins
claims.text: Iterating the map from (1, 0) with exact big integers: 10<sup>5</sup> passes, all covered by the map, so no halt. n then has 8,063 digits, and the index k never exceeded 1,046. Of the 3,880 Z-events, the tightest has n/(12k+12) = 55 (pass 28, n = 3,989, k = 5); after pass 70 the ratio is above 10<sup>6</sup>.

claims.title: Probviously non-halting: the index would have to catch up with n
claims.text: A halt can only start from Z<sub>k</sub> with n < 12k+12. In a phase of X/Y tails, k moves by −2 to +1 and is multiplied by 3/2 at 1 pass in 8, and it starts again from 0 at every phase. Along the orbit the fraction of Z-events with k ≥ K falls like K<sup>−1.1</sup> to K<sup>−1.7</sup> (0.6% for K = 100), while n grows by a factor of about 9/8 per pass. So the chance that some phase reaches k ≈ n/12 is about (n/12)<sup>−1.2</sup> per phase: about 10<sup>−5</sup> at the end of direct simulation, and far smaller after that, where n has thousands of digits.

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state E reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m modulo 2, 8 or 24 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (33 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 22 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 646 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 146,886 of the run (A = 1 04, U = 01, m = 90, B = (empty)): 646 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 192 bits (about 10117 steps of the machine). 81 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 1,049 cells. The iteration stops there, at a context too large for the six simulations (a second long block has formed); this is a limit of the tool, not an event of the machine.

claims.title: No halting class among 103 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 103 contexts expanded, 143 found, to depth 11. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 682 classes could not be computed (their six simulations disagree or are too long).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known, but very probably not. Unlike Antihydra-type machines, the bad region is not reached by a fair random walk: k would have to grow as fast as n. No simple invariant k ≤ f(n) is in sight: within a 9/8 phase the residues n mod 8 that drive k are themselves a (9n+c)/8 orbit, and since (9n+c)/8 is a bijection on residues, any finite sequence of residues occurs for some n. So a bound on k is a Collatz-type statement about this orbit. Of the 3·10<sup>5</sup> starts (1, n) with n < 3·10<sup>5</sup>, only n = 8, 11, 13, 15 reach the uncovered region within 200 passes.

explainer.lede: Probably never. The machine multiplies a number n by 3/2 or by 9/8 at each pass. A short word at the right end of the tape carries a second, much smaller counter, which mostly moves up or down by one and occasionally grows by half. Halting needs the small counter to catch up with the big one, and the big one is far ahead.

facts.text: The pass map, for every tail and every n outside the one region where a halt can start, in Lean's kernel.
No halt: the first 10<sup>5</sup> passes stay in the proved region (3,000 of them checked by the kernel alone).
The tightest margin between n and the bound 12k+12, at pass 28; after pass 70 it is above a million.

sections.heading: A big number and a small counter
html: Every so often the head is in state E at the left end, on six 0s, followed by n copies of 10 and a short tail word. The tail is 1, Xk = 000 (10)^k 1, Yk = 11 (01)^k or Zk = 000 (10)^k 0001.

</svg>

With the tail 1, one pass multiplies n by 3/2: n even gives (3n+6)/2 and the tail stays 1, n odd gives (3n+1)/2 and the tail X0. With an X or Y tail, a pass multiplies n by 9/8 and changes the small counter k according to n mod 8:

Here ×3/2 means that k becomes 3k/2+3 (tail X) when k is even, and (3k+1)/2 with the tail Z when it is odd. When k would go below 0, the tail goes back to 1. A Zk tail does one 3/2 pass that subtracts about 4.5k, then returns to 1 or X0. So the run alternates between phases of 3/2 passes and phases of 9/8 passes, during which a small counter wanders and sometimes grows. From blank tape, n = 0, 3, 5, 8, 12, 21, …, and n = 48,351 at step 2.1·1010.

sections.heading: Only if the small counter catches up
html: All of these rules hold for every n, except the Zk rule, which needs n ≥ 12k+12. Below that bound the tail turns into longer words and the machine can halt (for example from Z15 with n = 189). So the machine can only halt if, at some Z-event, the counter k is at least about n/12.

That is very unlikely. k starts again from 0 in every 9/8 phase, and it grows by half only at 1 pass in 8, with an even k, while n grows at every pass. In the run the tightest moment was pass 28 (n = 3,989, k = 5), with a margin of 55. After pass 70 the margin is above a million, and after 105 passes n has 8,063 digits while k has never passed 1,046.

sections.heading: The map is proved; the question is about one orbit
html:
• Every pass is proved. Lean's kernel checks that from every E-event (except Zk with n < 12k+12) the machine reaches the E-event the map predicts, in exactly the predicted number of steps. The proof is split into 83 cases (by tail and by n mod 8 or mod 2). Each case is a run of the symbolic simulator through a few sweeps, with the repeated part (three rounds of the 9/8 phase, or one of the 3/2 phase) done once and iterated by induction.
  • The orbit from blank tape is checked by evaluating the map in Lean: 3,000 passes in the kernel (more than 10450 steps), 105 passes compiled (1016000 steps), never entering the unproved region.
  • What is missing for a non-halting proof is an argument that k never catches up with n along the whole orbit. The residues of n that drive k are themselves a Collatz-like sequence, so this is as hard as the usual Collatz-type questions.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state E reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m modulo 2, 8 or 24 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 22 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 146,886 of the run (A = 1 04, U = 01, m = 90, B = (empty)): 646 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 192 bits (about 10117 steps of the machine). 81 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 1,049 cells. The iteration stops there, at a context too large for the six simulations (a second long block has formed); this is a limit of the tool, not an event of the machine.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 103 contexts expanded, 143 found, to depth 11. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 682 classes could not be computed (their six simulations disagree or are too long).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.128). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.41).
After 109 steps the tape spans 13,857 cells (61 left of the start, 9,722 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A Collatz-like map n -> 3n/2 or 9n/8 with a second counter k in the tail word that moves by -2..+1 or is multiplied by 3/2; the map is proved in Lean for every n except where the tail Z_k meets n < 12k+12, which needs k to catch up with n (orbit checked in Lean for 10^5 passes; probviously non-halting).
family: Two-level Collatz: n -> 3n/2 or 9n/8 with a tail counter k -> 3k/2
